differential.diagnosis: Weight gain due to smoking cessation

additional_considerations.rationale: Obesity has strong genetic influences, but a positive family history does not explain acute weight gain.
Must be suspected in any woman of childbearing age with unexplained weight gain, whatever the menstrual history.
Rare cause of unexplained weight gain; usually suggested on exam by hypertension, moon facies, plethora, fat pads, truncal obesity and striae.

source_issues: Doorway vital signs have no blood pressure (BMI 30 is given instead); the note's 'VS: WNL' cannot be checked against a doorway BP.
Notes for the SP contain only 'No.'; there are no stage directions.
p008: the open question 'How has your energy level been lately?' is answered 'No.'; resolved as no fatigue from the topic and the note ('denies ... fatigue') in f010.

The note puts dry skin and cold intolerance at 6 months; in the script the only 6-month onset (p014) is for the menstrual changes, and no duration is given for dry skin or feeling cold. The gold calls both 'chronic'. Added the note duration as from_note fact f006.
The note says 'Bipolar disorder, diagnosed 6 months ago'; the script says lithium was started 6 months ago and does not date the diagnosis.
The note omits the hair falling out (p004).
The challenging 'question' is a statement ('I want to resume smoking because I have begun to gain weight since I stopped.').
annotator_notes: persona.acting_notes is empty because the SP notes contain no directions ('No.').
'My appetite is good' (p007) is recorded literally as present; the note reads it as 'good appetite'.
Menstrual history is split into the former 4-week cycle (historical), the current 6-week-or-longer cycle, period length, 6-month onset of the changes, former and current pad use.
p030 diet is split into its separate statements (standard diet, unchanged for over a decade, coffee through the day, foods eaten, eating out).
Smoking: resolved current status (f042) plus historical exposure (f043), as in the worked example.
BMI 30 is kept as a doorway vital sign record (v004).
